findings.summary: The surface check lists files under scripts/ and packages/ only, while the kit carries six script files under corpus/, two of which call Git; their forms are at or below the floor, twelve recorded and apply --unidiff-zero not.

findings.reproduction: Git 2.48.0's and 2.50.0's release notes as installed with Git 2.55.0 (RelNotes/2.48.0.adoc line 118, RelNotes/2.50.0.adoc line 102) and Git 2.31.0's git-fsck.txt
findings.summary: The fsck fallback's stated premise, that a Git without --no-references checks no reference database, does not hold for Git 2.48 and 2.49, whose fsck checks references and has no such option.

processCorrections: One read-only inventory command held an unquoted pattern that matched no file, so zsh ran none of it; the search was repeated with the pattern quoted before any conclusion was drawn from it.

A first read of the planning session's scratch looked for Git 2.31.0's source there; the directory holds only the manual text, so the two manual readings this review cites (git-apply.txt and git-fsck.txt) come from that text and no source reading is claimed.
The exploratory corpus probe ran from session scratch with a plain temporary directory; the filed probe uses the repository's fixture-root helper and was run again from its committed path.

The first release surface check failed on this review's own release notes: a command written with an angle-bracket placeholder reads as raw HTML to the body profile. The placeholder was removed from the release notes and from the pull-request body, and the check then passed.

A check of generated artifacts was first asked of npm run sync with a flag it does not take; it printed its usage and changed nothing, which git status confirmed. The generated task of the document gate is that check.
